title: Why is AI-generated content called AI-slop, these days.
author: Specific-Animal6570

comments.author: _HoundOfJustice
comments.body: Partially due to ideological reasons but partially and im one of those as well - because people dont bother refining and working on top of the generated AI content. At best people spend more time in setting the workflow up in ComfyUI or similar than actually working on the image itself. There is ton of generic AI content with zero proper edits on color, AI mistakes and artifacts, composition and so on. Also it doesnt help that  ton of the content always circles around the same generic content - portraits of "hot" women and anime girls with exaggerated body parts and some other stuff filling platforms where AI content is being shared. Yeah, to me all of that is slop.

replies.author: lesuperhun
replies.body:
to add to that : some ai users are pretty cult-like in their opinion about ai, and don't take criticism too kindly, to put it mildly.

add to that a lot of scam-adjacent content made with ai, and a general poor public opinion about ai ( because it was officially made to take peeps jobs), while big moguls pretend this is the new big thing after computers, while ignoring any and all costs, inflating a big economic bubble and pretending it can do things it can't yet.

and you get two camps : the one who like ai, because it does thing they can't better than they can.  
and the experts in their domain, that realise ai is still far from doing anything close to a professional level.

so, when peeps come and reject any and all criticism under the umbrella of "luddite will call ai slop so it doesn't matter", it does help propagate the stereotype of "ai slop".

basically : ai slop as a name exist because some people are being dishonest and pretend it wasn't made by ai. I more rarely see "ai slop" name being used on ( good quality) content that assume being ai.

replies.author: _HoundOfJustice
replies.body: Yeah those are what i typically call AI bros. What makes it worse and more annoying is when they think they know how industries and fields work. Their source for their claims are AI gurus on social media + their cope and hope mechanism and both of them suck and are unreliable. Like okay i get the AI enthusiasm and i use the tech for the one or another purpose myself, but as a professional artist especially but also game dev and someone who networks a lot with pros and veterans in the industries (especially entertainment industry) i for sure dont have to listen to someone who has no foot in any of these how im supposed to ditch my workflows for AI and how something like ComfyUI is the future and Photoshop dying and so on. Those AI workflows are a toy compared to the workflows and pipelines of professionals but also hobbyist artists and devs to be honest.

replies.author: MysteriousPepper8908
replies.body: I think a lot of that is fair but how do you reconcile the professional use of AI by companies like Coca Cola with the idea that AI can't do anything at a professional level? You can debate as to whether it is a reduction in quality compared to their typical content but I would say "professional level" is defined by what is used by professional companies and not the other way around.

replies.author: lesuperhun
replies.body:
well, given the backlash and negative advertisement that coca cola ad led to, i'd say it was a pretty bad idea on their part.

a professionnal level is a level above amateur work. companies making slop doesn't make slop a professional level.

i'd never call a mc donald burger professional culinary level. and yet, it is undeniable designed by people doing it as a profession.

but anyway, what i call it doesn't really matter. debating about word use is pretty meaningless. what i call professional level of 'a thing' might be a bit closer to "understanding how it work enough to do the thing, and being able to do it in a trustworthy manner, without the need for an expert to double check your work".   
ie : if i were to ask a professional to do the thing, what level of quality am i expecting to receive ?

but semantics don't define what can be done by ai. what ai is able to do does. and right now, ai still need a lot of supervision, it isn't yet able to assess its own results as being " good" "acceptable", or just plain "wrong". it is able to give you "an answer that is likely close to the one you're looking for". and that isn't enough to be trustworthy. but that's a limit of the current statistical models used, not a hard limit on ai itself.

though, and i'll give ai that, some humans ain't able to do that either, so i'll still put AI above a bad employee. but given it lack the ability to check its work before submitting it as "good enough", it ain't reached the level of a good employee yet. ( except in some very specific tasks, like making a summary of a text. ai is good at that, by design, because that's what the models used were initially for)

replies.author: MysteriousPepper8908
replies.body:
That sounds more like your personal preference than any sort of objective standard for what constitutes professional level. I'd call a lot of what Hollywood puts out "slop" but that doesn't mean it isn't being released by large, well-founded studios. Professional cuisine isn't really a thing, since there are well-founded companies selling food with many different price points and expectations. We can use words like "haute cuisine" for culinary excellence, though companies like McDonald's are always going to have more market and mind share than the restaurants that produce food of that quality.


Your definition of professional seems to put the onus on the AI to be able to do the thing autonomously rather than for the professional using it to be able to wield it effectively which isn't the expectation for any other tool. Sure, AI used naively won't produce work that any reasonably large company would want to release which is why we need professionals using it as part of a workflow.

replies.body: Es ist halt auch oft Müll

It is not the case however, and most people just afraid from it so they try to dimminish it in any ways possible.

comments.author: Fun_Score5537
comments.body:
Because 99% of people that are posting AI generated content are doing it with the lowest amount of effort.


Write prompt, get image/video, post it.


It's the solid use of AI and additional tuning of it's content that just goes unnoticed as being AI. 


Example, if I'm doing pixel art and using AI, I could just take the first image produced and go with that. But I would rather spend an half hour in a image editing tool and clean up all of the pixels and errors to make sure that it looks coherent and logical.

comments.body: It's a term for people who hate AI.

comments.author: PetiteGousseDAil
comments.body:
You produce ai slop when you have no standards.

People hate low quality art and 99% of people who use ai are too under qualified to recognize good and bad quality art.

If you're Larian you can use ai and not produce ai slop. If you're a get rich quick "I don't need to study art to be good at it" type of person, chances are that you are producing ai slop.

It's all about being experienced enough to recognize quality and coherent work from ai generated art that looks okay at first glance but falls apart when you look at it for more than 2 sec

It's not a new thing. It's like the people that dislike bad CG in movies so therefore all CG is now bad.

replies.author: imnotabot303
replies.body:
Not really, people will eventually realise AI isn't just going to vanish because a minority of people complain about it on the internet. There's always going to be some people complaining though.

There is going to be a huge amount of "slop" churned out and there's not much that can be done about that. Although people like to call it AI slop it's actually just human slop. Whenever something is made easier and more accessible, people will use it to make low effort slop. It's just an unfortunate byproduct of technical progression.
